main.title: Population – scenario
main.help.tip: Opens the help page of the tab shown.
main.open.tip.title: Open…
main.open.tip: Loads a scenario file (.json) saved earlier.
main.save.tip.title: Save…
main.save.tip: Saves every setting to a .json file, to run exactly the same calculation later.
scenario.name: Name
scenario.name.tip.title: Name
scenario.name.tip: Used in the report and in the name of the result layer group.
scenario.language.tip.title: Report language
scenario.language.tip: Language of the report and table headers. File names stay in English.
scenario.output.tip.title: Output folder
scenario.output.tip: Each run is written in a dated sub-folder (for example 2026-09-29_144805): no result is ever overwritten. Runs that are not kept can be deleted at the end of the session.
grid.cell_size.tip.title: Cell size
grid.cell_size.tip: 250 m by default. Larger for a quick first run over a large extent; rarely below 250 m (several buildings per cell).
grid.density_unit.tip.title: Density unit
grid.density_unit.tip: Unit of the densities entered and published. The calculation stays consistent whatever the unit.
grid.crs.tip.title: Calculation CRS
grid.crs.tip: Always projected, in metres: areas are computed in m². Layers may use any CRS, they are reprojected. A CRS in degrees is refused. Above 0.5 % of area distortion, an equal-area CRS is recommended.
crs.project_not_metric: The project CRS is not in metres: the tool will use the raster's if metric, otherwise the UTM zone of the study area.
data.study_area.tip.title: Study area
data.study_area.tip: Administrative boundaries of the area to simulate.
data.typology.tip.title: Typology and class field
data.typology.tip: Layer of zones (rural, urban, high-end…) and the field holding the class. Class names are free.
data.admin_units.tip.title: Administrative units
data.admin_units.tip: Optional. For balances by unit and recalibration on projections.
data.raster.tip.title: Population raster
data.raster.tip: Raster at the base year, in any coordinate system (reprojected without losing inhabitants).
data.value_type.tip.title: Raster content
data.value_type.tip: Density (like the BUR71 raster) or inhabitants per pixel (like WorldPop). A mix-up would bias everything by the pixel area.
data.boundary.tip.title: Boundary pixels
data.boundary.tip: A pixel across the study-area boundary is cut: only the area inside is counted.
data.roofs.tip.title: Roofs (buildings)
data.roofs.tip: Google Open Buildings, PostGIS, GeoPackage… Used by the calibration (phase 6).
data.exclusions.tip.title: Exclusion zones
data.exclusions.tip: Forests, lakes, military areas, dams… as many layers as needed.
data.exclusions.name: Name
data.exclusions.behaviour.tip.title: Behaviour
data.exclusions.behaviour.tip: No inflow: its inhabitants stay, its growth moves elsewhere. Relocate: all its inhabitants move (dam). Outside: removed (other country, lake).
data.projections.file.tip.title: Projection file
data.projections.file.tip: CSV, Excel (xlsx, xls) or OpenDocument (ods). Either one row per unit and year (columns unit, year, population), or one row per unit and one column per year, as statistics offices publish them.
data.projections.use.tip.title: Use
data.projections.use.tip: Comparison only, yearly recalibration, or start on a projection year.
data.projections.start_year.tip.title: Start year
data.projections.start_year.tip: Only used when starting on a projection year.
time.base_year.tip.title: Base year
time.base_year.tip: Year of the base population (census year).
time.end_year.tip.title: Final horizon
time.time_step.tip.title: Time step
time.time_step.tip: 10, 5, 1 year or less. Output years are always reached exactly.
time.output_years.tip.title: Output years
time.output_years.tip: Years for which maps are written. Empty: at the end of every step.
time.output_years.placeholder: empty: every year computed; else e.g. 2030, 2040, 2050
time.frequency.tip.title: Migration
time.frequency.tip: Every year: better distribution. Once per step: faster, for a first try; reported.
time.first_migration_year.tip.title: First migration
time.first_migration_year.tip: Before this year, only growth applies.
parameters.key.tip.title: Class / zone
parameters.key.tip: Typology class name, parameter-zone identifier, or "*" for the default value.
parameters.extrapolation.tip.title: Beyond the years
parameters.extrapolation.tip: Before the first and after the last pivot year: constant value, or linear extension.
migration.k.tip.title: Neighbours
migration.k.tip: The excess of a cell goes in equal shares to the N nearest cells with free room.
migration.tolerance.tip.title: Tolerance (inhabitants)
migration.tolerance.tip: Minimal excess, in whole inhabitants, that triggers a move. No-inflow zones export all their excess.
migration.policy.tip.title: When room runs out
migration.policy.tip: What to do when the population no longer fits. See the help page on non-convergence.
migration.max_auto_increase.tip.title: Max automatic increase
migration.max_auto_increase.tip: Increase of maximum densities accepted without asking (0 %: always ask).
migration.sink_width_cells.tip.title: Ring width (cells)
migration.sink_width_cells.tip: Width of the ring of sink cells around the study area.
water.enabled.tip.title: Compute drinking-water demand
water.enabled.tip: Adds maps and totals of consumption, mean production, peak day and peak hour.
water.water_per_capita.tip.title: Allowance (l/cap/d)
water.water_per_capita.tip: Domestic consumption per inhabitant and per day.
water.non_domestic_share.tip.title: Non-domestic (%)
water.non_domestic_share.tip: Schools, health, shops… as % of domestic consumption.
water.non_domestic_volume.tip.title: Fixed volume (m³/d)
water.non_domestic_volume.tip: Fixed non-domestic needs of the zone, shared pro rata population.
water.network_efficiency.tip.title: Efficiency (%)
water.network_efficiency.tip: Network efficiency: applies to daily demand, not to the peak hour.
water.peak_day_factor.tip.title: Peak day
water.peak_hour_factor.tip.title: Peak hour
water.note: A value, or values by year: "2026: 20; 2040: 30".
indicators.other: Other uses (waste, energy, school places…) can be added here the same way.
run.run.tip.title: Run
run.run.tip: Checks the scenario and runs it in the background.
run.error: The run could not start: see the log.
run.status.success_with_adjustments: Run successful with adjustments (see the report).
run.status.partial: Partial run: part of the population could not be placed.
results.load.tip.title: Load layers
results.load.tip: Adds the checked maps to the project, in one group per scenario, with ready-made styles.
report.none: No report yet: run a scenario first.
nc.title: Not enough room in {year}
nc.raise: Raise maximum densities by {increase} % (minimum: {minimal} %), also for the following years
nc.sink: Place the excess in a ring of sink cells around the study area
nc.unallocated: Record the excess as unallocated population and go on
nc.note: The run restarts from the beginning with the chosen solution, which is recorded in the scenario and the report.
help.title: Help — Population
about.title: About Poplar
about.text:
Poplar — population growth and migration

Projects the spatial distribution of population year after year, by growth and migration under density constraints, and translates it into needs (drinking water…).

Version {version}
Origin: SHER tool (QGIS model and PyQGIS script), rebuilt in 2026 for project BUR71.
Authors: original tool, Keyvan; rebuild, Michel, with AI-assisted development (to be confirmed).
Method: code validated by automated tests and by comparison with the original tool.
Organisation, licence, contact: to be confirmed.
Dependencies: none beyond QGIS.

Project repository
processing.run.name: Run a scenario
processing.run.help: Runs a Poplar scenario file (.json): growth, migration and indicators from the base year to the final horizon. Results (rasters, summary.csv table, report) are written to the scenario's output folder or to the folder given.
processing.run.load: Load the final population and density
results.run.tip.title: Run shown
results.run.tip: Each run has its own folder. Choose the one whose maps, table and report you want to see.
results.kept.tip.title: Keep
results.kept.tip: A kept run is never proposed for deletion.
results.label.tip.title: Run name
results.label.tip: A short name to find it again, for example “reference” or “dmax + 20 %”.
results.clean.tip.title: Clean up
results.clean.tip: Deletes in one go the runs that are not kept.
cleanup.title: Clean-up of the results
cleanup.intro: Runs saved in {folder}. The runs checked in “Delete” are erased with their files; their layers are first removed from the project.
cleanup.intro_end: End of session: these runs take up space in {folder}. Check “Keep” to keep a run; the other checked runs will be deleted.
cleanup.all.tip.title: Check all
cleanup.all.tip: If no run is kept, the latest successful run stays unchecked.
cleanup.delete.tip.title: Delete selection
cleanup.delete.tip: Permanently erases the checked folders. Input data are never touched.
cleanup.failed:
Some files could not be deleted (open in another program?):
{files}
check.buffer_missing: Exclusion zone “{name}”: a layer of lines or points needs a buffer in metres (Data tab).
data.exclusions.buffer.tip.title: Buffer (m)
data.exclusions.buffer.tip: Width added around each feature, in metres. Required for a layer of lines (road, river) or points (borehole); optional for polygons, which it widens.
parameters.growth_rate.tip.title: Growth rate
parameters.growth_rate.tip: Annual growth rate in % per year, per zone of the chosen layer. Between pivot years the rate is interpolated; over a time step its mean applies.
parameters.dmax.tip.title: Maximum densities
parameters.dmax.tip: Density above which a cell takes nobody in; the surplus migrates to neighbouring cells. Per zone of the chosen layer, possibly varying over time.
parameters.zones.tip.title: Zones of the parameter
parameters.zones.tip: Polygon layer and field that delimit the zones of this parameter (typology, communes, provinces…). One row is created per value of the field. No layer: same value everywhere.
parameters.cross.tip.title: Cross two layers
parameters.cross.tip: Values per combination of two divisions, for example province × urban/rural type. A pair without a value takes the default.
parameters.default_row.tip.title: Default value
parameters.default_row.tip: Used for cells outside the zones of the layer, and for zones without a value.
parameters.remove_year.tip.title: Remove a pivot year
parameters.remove_year.tip: Deletes a year column and its values.
parameters.add_year.tip.title: Add a pivot year
parameters.add_year.tip: Adds a column: the value of the parameter in that year. Between years, linear interpolation.
parameters.import.tip.title: Import a table
parameters.import.tip: Reads a csv, xlsx, xls or ods file: a “zone” column (and “zone_2” when crossing), a “constant” column or one column per year.
parameters.export.tip.title: Export the table
parameters.export.tip: Saves the table as xlsx, ods or csv, to fill it in a spreadsheet and import it again.
parameters.import_error: The table could not be read: {error}
parameters.absent: Not in the layer: this value is not used.
data.projections.sheet.tip.title: Sheet
data.projections.sheet.tip: Sheet of the workbook to read.
data.projections.columns.tip.title: Columns
data.projections.columns.tip: Recognised from their names; set them if reading fails.
data.projections.unit_column.tip.title: Unit column
data.projections.unit_column.tip: Names or codes of the administrative units, identical to the field chosen for the administrative units.
data.projections.year_column.tip.title: Year column
data.projections.year_column.tip: Only for a table with one row per unit and year.
data.projections.value_column.tip.title: Population column
data.projections.value_column.tip: Only for a table with one row per unit and year.
main.library.tip.title: Scenario library
main.library.tip: Start from a scenario saved in the library, or add the current scenario to it.
scenario.description.tip.title: Description
scenario.description.tip: One sentence to find the scenario in the library: assumptions, source of the parameters…
library.title: Scenario library
library.change.tip.title: Library folder
library.change.tip: A shared folder (network drive) lets the whole team start from the same reference scenarios.
library.name: Name
library.empty: The library is empty: set up a scenario, then click “Add the current scenario…”.
library.add.tip.title: Add to the library
library.add.tip: Saves a copy of the scenario of the window in the library, with a name and a description.
library.open.tip.title: Start from this scenario
library.open.tip: Loads the scenario in the window as a new scenario: the original in the library is not changed.
layers.browse.tip.title: Add a layer
layers.browse.tip: Choose a file (shapefile, GeoPackage, GeoTIFF…) or a database layer (PostGIS, GeoPackage, SpatiaLite): it is added to the project and selected.
layers.sublayer_label: This file holds several layers; which one should be used?
layers.invalid: The layer “{name}” could not be opened.
layers.unsupported: The layer “{name}” (source {provider}) cannot be read by the calculation engine: save it as a GeoPackage (right click › Export › Save Features As…).
layers.wrong_type: The layer “{name}” does not have the right geometry type for this list (polygons are expected).
tab.calibration.tip: Roofs, strata, census and inhabitants per roof.
calibration.use_roofs: Starting population computed from the roofs (instead of the raster of the Data tab)
calibration.use_roofs.tip.title: Starting population
calibration.use_roofs.tip: Unchecked: the population raster of the Data tab. Checked: the roofs calibrated below; the raster, if given, only aligns the grid.
calibration.roof_layer.tip.title: Roof layer
calibration.roof_layer.tip: Polygons (area computed) or points with an area field, from a file or a database.
calibration.roof_file.tip.title: Google Open Buildings
calibration.roof_file.tip: CSV tile (possibly compressed) of Google Open Buildings: read directly, not through QGIS. Takes precedence over the layer.
calibration.area_field.tip.title: Roof area
calibration.area_field.tip: Area field in m²; empty: area computed from the polygon, in the calculation CRS.
calibration.usage_field.tip.title: Roof usage
calibration.usage_field.tip: Field of usage categories, read as it is in the data. Each category gets a coefficient (Coefficients… button).
calibration.confidence.tip.title: Confidence threshold
calibration.confidence.tip: Off by default. On: roofs below the threshold are left out (Google Open Buildings: confidence column).
calibration.roof_year.tip.title: Imagery year
calibration.roof_year.tip: Year of the imagery the roofs were drawn from: used by the suggested growth rate and the report.
calibration.strata_layer.tip.title: Calibration strata
calibration.strata_layer.tip: Polygons that each have a census population (communes…). Empty: the whole study area is one stratum.
calibration.group_field.tip.title: Regression group
calibration.group_field.tip: Field grouping the strata that share one curve (rural / urban type…). Empty: one curve per stratum.
calibration.census_field.tip.title: Census field
calibration.census_field.tip: Field of the strata layer holding the census population; fills the table.
calibration.census_table.tip.title: Known population
calibration.census_table.tip: Population of each stratum (census, or validated projection), editable.
calibration.census_year.tip.title: Year of the known population
calibration.census_year.tip: Year of the census or of the validated projection.
calibration.target_year.tip.title: Target year
calibration.target_year.tip: Year of the starting population; by default the start year of the scenario. The known population is carried to it with the gap growth rate.
calibration.gap_rate.tip.title: Gap growth rate
calibration.gap_rate.tip: Rate carrying the known population to the target year. Empty: the default growth rate of the scenario.
calibration.recalibrate: Apply the recalibration on the known population
calibration.recalibrate.tip.title: Recalibration
calibration.recalibrate.tip: The recalibration factor is always computed and shown; it is applied only when this box is checked (factor 1 by default).
calibration.compute.tip.title: Calibrate
calibration.compute.tip: Reads the roofs, links them to the strata and fits every group. Afterwards every setting of the group reacts at once.
calibration.done: {read} roofs read, {kept} kept, {outside} outside the study area.
calibration.no_roofs: Choose a roof layer or file first.
calibration.method.tip.title: Shape of the curve
calibration.method.tip: Steps: every roof gets the whole number of inhabitants of its class. Segments or polynomial: continuous curve between the classes.
calibration.cut.tip.title: Class cut
calibration.cut.tip: Natural breaks: follow the gaps of the distribution. Equal areas: classes of the same width. Percentiles: classes of the same size (advised for the regression on several strata). Manual: limits moved on the chart.
calibration.n_classes.tip.title: Number of classes
calibration.n_classes.tip: The cut and the fit are redone at each change.
calibration.floor.tip.title: Floor
calibration.floor.tip: Smaller roofs hold nobody (shelters, annexes). Percentile of the areas (1st by default), value in m², or none.
calibration.ceiling.tip.title: Ceiling
calibration.ceiling.tip: End of the last class; larger roofs take the value of the last class. Percentile (90th by default), value in m², or none.
calibration.exclude_above.tip.title: Large buildings
calibration.exclude_above.tip: Above, a roof holds nobody (non-residential building). Unchecked: no exclusion.
calibration.area_per_person.tip.title: Roof area per inhabitant
calibration.area_per_person.tip: Inhabitants proposed for a class = mean roof area of the class ÷ this area, rounded.
calibration.fit.tip.title: Fit to the census
calibration.fit.tip: Finds the roof area per inhabitant that gives the known population of the group best, with whole inhabitants.
calibration.min_per_roof.tip.title: Minimum per roof
calibration.min_per_roof.tip: At least this many inhabitants for every roof kept.
calibration.max_per_roof.tip.title: Maximum per roof
calibration.max_per_roof.tip: At most this many inhabitants for a roof.
calibration.overridden: Value changed by hand (recorded in the report)
calibration.totals: Computed population {population} · known population {census} · gap {gap} % · proposed recalibration {factor}
calibration.totals_alert: Computed population {population} · known population {census} · gap {gap} %, beyond ±{alert} %: fit or recalibrate (proposed factor {factor})
calibration.totals_no_census: Computed population {population} · no known population: the area per inhabitant is not fitted
calibration.reference.tip.title: Reference roof area per inhabitant
calibration.reference.tip: Value from elsewhere (another calibrated commune, an earlier study): the tool derives a growth rate between the imagery year and the year of the known population.
calibration.tcam: Growth rate suggested with {reference} m² per inhabitant: {rate} % per year. If it differs much from the default growth rate, one of the two assumptions needs a review.
calibration.tcam_none: Suggested growth rate: give the imagery year, the year of the known population and a reference area.
report.open_html.tip.title: Full report
report.open_html.tip: Self-contained report with charts and calibration, to open in a browser, printable to PDF.
